thread:
maria: Heads-up — the onboarding sampleapp is spiking 429s and returning duplicate pagination cursors under burst. Repro steps at the end.
aj: Ugh. Is this coming from client-side throttling or the server?
devon: I saw similar yesterday. JS SDK defaults to a leaky-bucket window that batches too aggressively on short bursts. Python uses semaphore + queue so it smooths differently.
sam: Can you paste the client config?
maria: Sure — minimal repro config:
```js
// sampleapp config
const client = new Redwood({
  apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY,
  throttle: { windowMs: 1000, maxRequests: 25 }, // bursty
  paginator: { pageSize: 50 }
});
```
maria: Logs from the test run: 
```
[sampleapp] 2026-03-20T15:02:01Z ERROR 429 TooManyRequests route=/v1/generate id=abc123
[sampleapp] 2026-03-20T15:02:01Z WARN  paginated cursor duplicated: cursor=\"eyJpZCI6M...\"
[sampleapp] 2026-03-20T15:02:02Z INFO  retrying request id=abc123 attempt=1 backoff=150ms
```
aj: That duplicate cursor is concerning — sounds like the client re-requested a page while the server was still processing and returned the same token. Could be auth/retry interplay.
devon: Right. We found that when a 401 happens mid-page, the JS SDK does an auth refresh then replays the request without marking it idempotent; server returns the page again and the sampleapp merges it, causing dupes.
sam: Is the behavior different in Go SDK?
devon: Go uses request IDs + a lightweight dedupe table in the paginator. JS/Python lack that by default.
alex: Proposed short fixes:
- add idempotency token to paginator requests (header X-Redwood-Page-ID)
- unify backoff jitter to base=100ms with expo cap=2s across SDKs
- adjust default throttle window to 500ms/10req to reduce burst blasting
maria: I sketched a quick patch in the sampleapp that adds a page-id:
```diff
- await client.fetchPage({cursor})
+ await client.fetchPage({cursor, headers: { 'x-redwood-page-id': `${sessionId}:${pageSeq}` }})
```
maria: With that, duplicate merges stop in my run.
aj: Good find. Can we make this a platform recommendation? Also need parity: JS + Python should expose a small paginator hook so apps can opt into dedupe.
devon: I'll open two issues: one for SDK parity (paginator idempotency API) and one for default config changes. I'll include perf numbers.
ci-bot: devon opened issue #devex/1534: "paginator idempotency + SDK parity"
sam: For the short term, docs: add a note to the onboarding sampleapp readme about burst-safe configs and the auth-retry caveat.
alex: Also add a tiny integration test in sampleapp that simulates token refresh mid-page and asserts no duplicate items.
maria: Repro steps I used: run 20 parallel workers requesting consecutive pages with pageSize=50 for 60s, hit with expired API key at t+10s to force refresh. Capture logs.
aj: Thanks — I'll update the quickstart and drop a patch to the JS SDK default throttle.
maria: Thanks team :thumbsup: — leaving the log and a snippet in the sampleapp issue for whoever picks this up.
